title: A little time with the walls
excerpt: There is something about seeing a painting in person: the colour, the texture, the way it changes as you step back. A photograph primes the imagination. Standing in front of a painting is another thing entirely. And speaking of smiling.
Three paintings by Dave from the Robert and Maryann Ness collection are also hanging in the White Gallery. They offer a way to support something close to home.

title: A good conversation tonight
alt: Portrait from the letter about Good Conversations with Janice Wing
excerpt: Janice brings a life of experience in education, public service and community leadership. That gives us plenty to talk about, but what interests me most is the person behind all that doing. The people, places and relationships that have shaped her. Who she is becoming, and what she is paying attention to now.
That is why I love these conversations. We come together, listen, and sometimes leave with questions we hadn't thought to ask ourselves.

title: To home, with love and pasta
excerpt: I also brought something home you can eat. Anywhere I could find pesto I had it. In fact there is risk of my turning green. In Genova, there is an entire fleet of vans dedicated to delivering basil.

This Wednesday we're trying Pasta Take-Away. Gemelli al pesto, Crema di funghi, or Bolognese, $9 each with grissini, ready for pick-up from 11 a.m. Loraine and I worked together on Sunday and made a plan for Wednesday, and today we're already taking orders.

title: Fall, Balance, and Becoming
alt: David J. More artwork used in the equinox letter
excerpt: One story from my conversation with Dave More has stayed with me ever since we talked. On July 14, 2000, Dave was painting a towering summer cloud near Benalto. For reasons he still can't explain, he reached into his paint box, loaded his brush with deep red, and swept it through the middle of the cloud.
The colour troubled him, but he left it. Later that evening he learned that the very cloud he'd been painting all afternoon had drifted southeast and become the Pine Lake tornado.

title: Tomorrow.
alt: Three David J. More paintings hanging under a sheet in the White Gallery
excerpt: A little of their history, in Dave's own words. The three are Twilight at Parlee, New Brunswick (2020), Last Sail at Parlee (2021), and Passage — Bay of Chaleur, which he finished only this past spring; parts of its surface were still soft in August.

The first two began on a September evening in 2014, when Dave and Yvette climbed the dunes above Parlee Beach to watch the sun settle. The sea took on a mantle of jade; the retreating tide left pools where the shadows glowed crimson and orange.

title: Dave More and more...
alt: The White Gallery wall with three David J. More paintings waiting to be unveiled
excerpt: At the heart of the opening, the chairs come out. We'll film Episode 8 of Good Conversations with Paul: Dave and I sit down in front of his work, and go where this series loves to go — belonging, becoming, and what can shape a life when you pay attention to it.
An artist in conversation, surrounded by paintings that no one — except Dave and his curators — has seen until this weekend. That doesn't happen often in any city.
